newsitem.title: USA: Fla. zoo employee stands in as marsupial mother.
newsitem.headline: Fla. zoo employee stands in as marsupial mother.

text.p: An employee at Florida's Dreher Park Zoo is so fond of the animals in her care that she takes on the role of surrogate mother to baby kangaroos.
Teri Blake, a commissary manager at the West Palm Beach zoo, has agreed to carry an orphaned baby kangaroo named Edie in a pack tied to her belly, simulating the pouch of a mother kangaroo.

For three months Blake will carry the pack all day, everywhere she goes. Her only breaks will be during Edie's brief daily play periods outside the pack and at night, when she hangs the pack -- equipped with a heating pad -- from her bathtub faucet, close to the ground so the baby will not get hurt if she falls out.
Blake began carrying Edie shortly after her mother died at the zoo from an infection two weeks ago. Female kangaroos will not adopt stranded babies, known as "joeys."
This is the second kangaroo surrogacy for Blake. Five years ago she carried another joey for six months after it was rejected by its mother. That kangaroo did very well, she said.
Edie will be eight months old when she leaves Blake's care. Baby kangaroos typically stay in their mother's pouches for a year but Blake said eight months would be long enough for Edie.

Blake said she did not expect to have a problem letting go of her surrogate child. "I'm happy to do it, but I just want to raise her and put her back with the rest," Blake told the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel.
